outcome: Clinical applications get a faster, more reliable network path with security enforced at the same device, everywhere at once.
overview: A unified health record only works if every facility can reach it quickly and securely, and traditional wide-area networking gives you one or the other. A UAE healthcare operator needed both, and after assessment and proof-of-concept work with partner CNS Middle East deployed Fortinet Secure SD-WAN: application-aware path selection over multiple circuits with security enforced at the same device. The assessment and proof-of-concept phases are the notable part — clinical connectivity is not a place to discover that an overlay behaves differently under load than it did on paper.

benefits.text: Clinical application traffic is steered onto the best-performing available path rather than a fixed route
benefits.limits: The published reference describes one named customer engagement. It is evidence that Redington has delivered this, and it is not a performance figure that transfers to the next customer

benefits.text: Connectivity and security are enforced at one device per facility rather than two stacks
benefits.limits: Consolidation concentrates failure as well as management; facility-level resilience must be designed rather than assumed

benefits.text: Additional circuits can be used productively instead of sitting idle as standby
benefits.limits: The same operating system runs on the appliance, as a virtual machine and in cloud, so the capability claim survives a form-factor change; the throughput figure behind it does not, and must be re-sized per form factor

residency: Overlay, policy and logs stay within the operator’s estate; clinical traffic does not transit a third-party inspection service in this design

notFor.situation: An operator already running an SD-WAN overlay from another vendor
notFor.why: Overlays do not interwork, so a second one means running two networks during a long transition

notFor.situation: A single-site operator with no wide-area requirement
notFor.why: There are no paths to select between

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Fortinet implementation partner; the referenced engagement was delivered with partner CNS Middle East · Duration: 12–18 weeks including a proof-of-concept phase that is not compressible
Support model: Vendor hardware and subscription support with a replacement term appropriate to clinical criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed overlay operations.
1) Assessment — circuit inventory and diversity verification, application classification review, facility throughput measurement
2) Proof of concept — representative facilities on the overlay with classification validated against real traffic
3) Design — overlay topology, per-application policy, hub sizing and rollout order
4) Roll out and hand over — facilities migrated, central management established, operations handed over
deliverables: Clinical application traffic is observed taking the better path when circuit quality diverges
A single circuit failure at a facility does not interrupt a clinical session, verified by test
Per-application path quality is reportable per facility
